correctness.rationale: The normalized Walsh basis turns concentration into an exact (n+1)-dimensional Gram matrix with diagonal p, off-coordinate entries s and off-coordinate-pair entries t. The permutation-standard sector is p-t with multiplicity n-1; the two-dimensional radial sector has the stated characteristic polynomial. Direct conditional-binomial identities and t/s=(n-1-2r)/(n-1) prove strict interior interlacing; evaluation on radius-one vertices proves positivity, while contractivity gives eigenvalues <=1. Binomial central and local limit theorems and an exact central-binomial ratio give the claimed Gaussian limiting levels and decreasing half-ball singular-value condition numbers. Extracted standalone finite checker exhaustively compared all 39 matrices for 3<=n<=8, recomputed rational characteristic polynomials by a distinct exact Newton-identity method, verified 99 exact monotonicity identities, and checked three CLT parameters; computations corroborate, but do not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The primary sources establish spherical-mean Fourier diagonalization, general graph spectral concentration, hypercube Slepian operators and their multiplicity/rank/eigenspace decompositions, and induced-Hamming-ball adjacency spectra. Hogan–Lakey already implies injectivity of the first-band restriction for ball radius >=1, and general projections yield the Slepian setup; those observations are not claimed novel. Their full first hypercube paper supplies numerical eigenvalues and general full rank but no all-radius closed first-band binomial formula or Gaussian two-outlier continuum with balanced condition-number monotonicity. The second paper restricts its detailed eigenspace construction to equal spatial/spectral radii and gives a finite matrix algorithm, not an all-radius closed scalar spectral identity. The stated formula and asymptotic transition are not implied as mathematical propositions by the inspected primary results. Residual risk of equivalent classical covariance/Krawtchouk formulas remains, so no independent novelty guarantee is asserted.
residual_risks: Older unindexed Boolean covariance, Krawtchouk or discrete prolate literature might contain an equivalent exact first-chaos binomial spectrum without using Slepian terminology.

The generic graph Slepian machinery and Hogan–Lakey numerical spectra may make the elementary lowest-band calculation accessible; the new contribution is a closed all-radius formula plus asymptotic and condition-number structure, not the construction of the concentration operator or known rank theorem.

value.rationale: The natural lowest nonconstant Walsh/Fourier subspace on a Boolean cube and its full family of Hamming balls are canonical, rather than an arbitrarily selected slice. Beyond the prior operator definition and rank theorem, the complete sharp eigenvalues determine optimal sampling distortion for each ball, establish a three-sector interlacing law and reveal a nontrivial two-outlier Gaussian Hermite limit as dimension grows. The odd-halfball condition number decreases strictly to an explicit constant. These are uniform structural statements over all dimensions/radii with concrete stable-sampling use; the calculation is elementary in its symmetry reduction but not merely a chosen numerical table or renaming of a known exact invariant.
